name: absgs-3k
question: Does AbsGS densification (absolute 2-D gradients) improve novel-view quality, in particular on glass, contours and furniture, relative to the default criterion?
modification: only the densification criterion: strategy.absgrad = true and grow_grad2d = 0.0008 (one method; gsplat states the threshold must be raised with absgrad); everything else identical
reference: AbsGS: Recovering Fine Details for 3D Gaussian Splatting (arXiv 2404.10484)
validation_panoramas: two (R0010006 and the panorama moved by the extended split)
design: paired: for each seed 0, 1, 2 a baseline and an AbsGS arm, 3000 steps, same schedule (densification i = 600..2400, no large-Gaussian pruning, position LR decay over 3000 steps, SH degree <= 2)

metrics.primary: paired difference AbsGS - baseline of mean validation PSNR and SSIM at 3000, overall and per validation panorama
secondary: region PSNR (glass, contours, furniture, mirror, unvalidated reflective)
Gaussian count, large and out-of-box (opaque) Gaussians

reading: mean, median, standard deviation and signs over seeds, read against the replicate noise; no winner on mean PSNR alone
not_used: test set R0010008, R0010014 (reserved; evaluate-test --final not run)
